# Ingest is idempotent on `(owner_id, source, name_key)`, with `name_key` generated by Postgres

Every Source writes through one function, `persistProfiles` in `db/ingest.ts`, and re-running a
Source has to be safe: the SEC filing index, Show HN and an accelerator's pages will all be
fetched again next week, and most of what comes back will be companies already in the Deck. The
natural key that makes the second run an update rather than a duplicate is the owner, the Source
name, and the company name reduced to what identity actually depends on — case-folded, with runs
of whitespace collapsed and the ends trimmed.

That reduction is a `GENERATED ALWAYS AS ... STORED` column rather than a value the write path
computes. The write path runs under the secret key, which per CLAUDE.md bypasses RLS, so a
mistake there is a mistake nothing else catches; a generated column cannot disagree with the
`name` beside it whoever did the writing, and it gives `on conflict` something to infer an index
from. `created_at` is deliberately not touched on update, because the Deck is ordered newest
first and re-ingesting a Source should not reshuffle it.

Inserted and updated are counted apart using Postgres's own `xmax = 0`, which is zero on a
freshly inserted tuple and carries a transaction id on one `do update` replaced. Reading the
table first and diffing would answer the same question one race later.

## Considered Options

**A key without the Source: one Profile per company name, whoever found it.** Tempting, because
it is the Deck that suffers from duplicates and the Deck does not care which pipeline found a
company. Rejected: two Sources agreeing on a name is not the same as two Sources describing the
same company, and under that key whichever ran last would silently overwrite the other's
`sector`, `stage` and provenance with no record that it had. Reconciling two Sources' accounts of
one company is entity resolution, it needs a rule for which field wins, and it is not a thing to
decide inside "write the row". The cost is accepted and real: a company found by two Sources is
two cards in the Deck until some later Ticket takes that on.

**A Source-supplied external id — the YC slug, the SEC CIK — as the key.** Genuinely stabler than
a name: a company that renames itself keeps its CIK. Rejected for now because there is no field
for it. `ProfileInput` carries name, description, sector, stage and website and nothing else, and
adding an opaque per-Source identifier to the schema every path shares, before a single Source
Ticket has landed to say what its identifier looks like, is guessing. Nothing here blocks it:
adding the column later changes the unique index and this function, and the generated `name_key`
stays as the fallback for Sources that have no such id.

**The raw `name` as the key, with no normalisation.** Rejected: `profileInputSchema` does not
trim, so " Sprocket" and "Sprocket" are both valid input, and a Source that changes its
whitespace or capitalisation would deal the Deck a second copy of every company it knows.

**Deduplicating in TypeScript — read the existing rows, then insert what is missing.** Rejected:
it is the same rule written twice, and the version Postgres does not know about is the one that
stops being true. A unique index is also what makes the guarantee survive a second process, which
matters the day ingest is run twice by mistake.

## Consequences

`profiles` gains two columns. `source` is not a Profile field and carries no provenance — it says
which pipeline produced the record, not what kind of value a field is, which is the distinction
`CONTEXT.md` draws between Source and Provenance. `name_key` is generated, so nothing may write
it; `$inferInsert` leaves it out and Postgres rejects it if something tries.

Migration `0002` adds `source` as `NOT NULL` with no default, which only applies to an empty
table. That is true here — this is the first write path into `profiles`, and nothing before it
has ever inserted a row outside a test — and a default would have been worse: `'unknown'` is a
Source name that would then be part of some rows' identity forever.

`persistProfiles` issues one statement per record rather than one multi-row insert, because
Postgres refuses to let a single `on conflict do update` affect the same row twice and two
records in one batch can reduce to the same key. Batches are a page of Source results at a time,
so the round trips are not the constraint; if that changes, the fix is to group by `name_key`
first, not to drop the constraint.

Ticket #136 narrowed what `do update` replaces. A field whose stored provenance is `jack` keeps
its value and its provenance; every other field takes the incoming scrape's. That choice is a
`case` per column and a per-field `jsonb_build_object` for `provenance`, inside the same
statement, for the reason the rest of this ADR gives: reading the row first would let two
ingest Runs both read `scraped` and race to overwrite a correction. A row whose every field is
`jack` still counts as updated, since `do update` writes a new tuple whether or not a value
changed.
